department: Department of Earth and Planetary Science

deadline.quote: Our application deadline for the 2027-2028 academic year is December 1, 2026 (8:59pm PST)

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

fee_waiver.value: Fee waivers are for US citizens/residents, but for international applicants a prospective advisor may sometimes pay the $155 fee; ask well before the deadline.
fee_waiver.quote: If you are an international applicant and cannot afford to pay the application fee, prospective faculty advisors might, in some cases, be able to pay your application fee from their own funds

supervisor.value: You are admitted directly into an advisor's research group and must pick at least one advisor; contacting faculty is strongly recommended.
supervisor.quote: Students are simultaneously admitted to the EPS Ph.D. program and to the research group of a faculty advisor, so the online application requires you to select at least one advisor.

also.quote: It is strongly recommended to contact professors you are interested in working with.

funding.value: Admitted students receive a funding package (fellowships, teaching, research appointments) covering fees, nonresident tuition and a stipend.
funding.quote: Upon admission to the PhD program, prospective students are provided a detailed funding package that specifies the length of funding and source of financial support.

entry_route.quote: We accept applicants with masters degrees, but they are not required for admission.

notes: All EPS PhD students must teach as a GSI for two semesters (higher English speaking standard).
